title: Merge Intervals
summary: Combine every group of overlapping intervals into one and return the non-overlapping result.

tests.explain: [1, 4] and [2, 6] overlap and become [1, 6]. [8, 10] and [9, 12] become [8, 12]. The two groups don't touch.
The input isn't sorted. [1, 3] and [3, 5] share the point 3, which counts as overlapping, and [5, 7] shares 5 with [3, 5], so everything merges into [1, 7].
[1, 10] already contains both of the other intervals.

hints: If the intervals were sorted by start, which intervals could a given interval possibly overlap with?
Sort by start. Keep the last interval of your answer open: each new interval either overlaps it (start <= its end) or starts a new group.
When they overlap, extend the end to the max of the two ends, not just the new end: [1, 10] followed by [2, 3] must stay [1, 10].

complexity.time: O(n log n): sorting, then one linear pass
complexity.space: O(n) for the output (plus the sort's own space)
